Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Houston/Galveston TX
507 AM CDT Mon Aug 3 2026

...New AVIATION...

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Couldn't rule out patchy dense fog this morning. 

- Hot summer weather through the forecast period. 

- Isolated afternoon shower/storm possible first half of week.
  Somewhat better chance of an afternoon shower/storm later in the
  week. 

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 1116 PM CDT Sun Aug 2 2026

A mid/upper ridge over SW CONUS is amplifying northeastward, with
its axis extending into the northern U.S. plains and central 
Canada. A deep-layer trough remains in place over E CONUS, with 
very dry mid/upper air pushing southward between the trough and 
the ridge. Even at the surface, very low dew points have pushed 
into our region in the wake of relatively weak sfc cold front. The
front has stalled near the coast, becoming increasingly diffused.
We'll likely continue the dry LL regime on Monday, featuring 
low/mid 60s dew points north of I-10 and 70s dew points near the 
coast. However,the sea breeze boundary is expected to push further
inland Monday afternoon, bringing higher dew points farther 
inland later in the day. Couldn't rule out an isolated afternoon 
shower or storm along the sea breeze boundary. We've actually 
dialed back on the hot temperatures a tad, making me glad we 
didn't totally buy into those 102-104 degree temperatures the NBM 
was suggesting a few days ago. But we are still calling for 
temperatures near 100 degrees inland, and low 90s at the coast. If
the sea breeze is delayed, then we can get a little hotter. 

The mid/upper flow pattern is expected to become less amplified as 
the week progresses. The E CONUS trough should erode north, while
the ridge to our west expands, increasing mid/upper pressure 
heights over Texas. Global ensemble mean 500 MB heights shows 
values increasing from roughly ~588dam to ~594dam between now and 
week's end. One's initial reaction to this trend would be the 
expectation of building heat. But as the E CONUS troughing fades 
away, our LL pattern will become more influenced by high pressure 
to the east, establishing deep onshore flow. This will have a 
tendency to increase the chance of late morning and afternoon 
cumulus, and could potentially increase the risk of a few 
isolated afternoon showers/storms. Therefore, afternoon high 
temperatures are actually forecast to decrease somewhat later this
week (still quite hot in the mid 90s). However, persistent 
onshore flow will likely increase dew points as well. So expect an
increasingly humid environment as the week progresses. Global 
ensembles keep PWAT anomalies below average, thus the PoPs 
remaining low all week. 

Self

&&

.AVIATION...
(12Z TAF Issuance)
Issued at 507 AM CDT Mon Aug 3 2026

Light and variable winds will persist through most of the morning
before becoming southerly to southeasterly in the afternoon hours.
Terminals closer to the coast will start out with light south-
southwesterly winds before transitioning to southeasterly winds
around 10 kt this afternoon. Cannot rule out intermittent periods
of patchy fog over the next few hours this morning in LBX/SGR. 
Isolated SH/TS possible this afternoon around the Houston metro 
terminals between 20Z-01Z, but the potential is too low to include
it in any of the TAFs. Brief periods of patchy fog will be 
possible again early Tuesday morning. 

Batiste

&&

.MARINE...
Issued at 1116 PM CDT Sun Aug 2 2026

Light to moderate winds and low seas are expected through the
forecast period. Winds on Monday are expected to be west to
southwest, before becoming more southerly as we approach mid week.
By the end of the week, winds are expected to become more
southeasterly. Isolated shower or storm possible along the sea
breeze boundary during the first half of the week. Somewhat better
chance of a shower/storm in the afternoon for the bays, and in the
morning hours in the Gulf later in the week.

&&

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Lake Charles LA
1232 PM CDT Mon Aug 3 2026

...New DISCUSSION, AVIATION, MARINE, FIRE WEATHER...

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Dewpoints will begin to rise through the work week, while both
  high and low temperatures are forecast to remain at or slightly
  above average.

-Isolated diurnally driven afternoon thunderstorms will be
 possible each day through the work week, with rain chances in the
 15 to 30% range.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
(This evening through next Sunday)
Issued at 1229 PM CDT Mon Aug 3 2026

Yesterday's weak boundary remains draped along the I-10 corridor 
this afternoon, providing light and variable winds across the 
forecast area. The boundary will continue its slow meander north 
towards the Ark-La-Miss through the early work week, allowing 
onshore flow to eventually become re-established once again. This 
will allow for a slow but steady increase in moisture through the 
next couple of days, with PWATs expected to return to near the 
50th percentile (~1.80" according to SPC climo) by Wednesday. 
Aloft, troughing over the E CONUS will gradually lift north today,
leaving behind a weak cutoff low over the SE CONUS. This low will
linger nearby into Wednesday, preventing upper ridging from 
taking hold for a while longer. With some additional upper level 
support nearby, a slight increase in afternoon rain chances is 
expected tomorrow and Wed, especially across the eastern parts of 
the CWA closer to the influence of the upper low.

By Thursday the upper low will be fully dissipated, with upper 
ridging over both the Four Corners region and the western Atlantic 
beginning to strengthen to our west and east simultaneously. Still, 
at this point guidance is in good agreement that these two ridges 
won't quite reach each other until possibly beyond the end of this 
forecast period, leaving a small weakness between them overhead 
through next weekend. At the surface, a well established onshore 
flow around a SE CONUS surface high will allow for even better 
moisture return through this same period, with PWATs increasing 
into/above the 75th percentile range. With decent moisture available 
and a slight weakness aloft, the chance for afternoon showers and 
storms will increase a bit further each day Thurs through Sun. 

&&

.AVIATION...
(18Z TAFS)
Issued at 1229 PM CDT Mon Aug 3 2026

Scattered to broken cloud deck near 5000 ft will continue to
stream across the region into this evening, thinking
out/dissipating overnight. Light and variable winds near 0-5kts 
will continue at all sites through the period. 

&&

.MARINE...
Issued at 1229 PM CDT Mon Aug 3 2026

A light west to southwest flow will continue through the next couple 
of days, becoming more southerly by late Tuesday and beyond. A few 
isolated showers will be possible later in the period, but overall 
mostly dry conditions are expected through the work week.

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Issued at 1229 PM CDT Mon Aug 3 2026

Minimum afternoon RH values are expected to range from 35 to 55 
percent once again today, amid a light and variable onshore flow. 
Moisture begins to slowly return today through the mid-week, 
allowing min RH values to return to the 50-60% range each day. 
Increasing moisture will bring back a chance for isolated afternoon 
thunderstorms again Tuesday and beyond.

&&
